accounting.rationale: Original PDF133 defines the possibility of external reference/definition/undefinition and additional pointer/allocatable property changes. It requires no particular external event and supplies no memory-layout, thread, atomicity, synchronization or timing oracle.
The means are not specified by the program. An ordinary Fortran assignment, a remote-image operation, a C-looking name or a delay alone is not independent evidence of this premise.
The object may be referenced externally; source accounting does not demonstrate that a processor/environment performed such a reference.
External definition is possible, not a mandate to generate it or a portable value/visibility oracle. A future experiment needs an independently justified actual external mechanism.
External undefinition does not authorize reading undefined data. Zero-sized/zero-length definedness and valid state inquiries retain19.6.2/16.1 ownership.
The additional pointer possibility concerns association status. It is not an assertion that a current status is defined or that ASSOCIATED is always permitted.
A pointer's dynamic type may change by external means. No guessed descriptor layout, representation cast or undefined-state inquiry is justified.

The pointer branch explicitly includes type parameters. Meaningful future observations need a processor-qualified mechanism and the required live/defined properties, not arbitrary raw-memory mutation.
Pointer array bounds may change externally. This is not a guarantee of association or permission to inquire disassociated/undefined bounds.
The additional allocatable possibility is allocation status, distinct from pointer association status. No allocation is implied merely by the attribute.
The allocatable branch includes dynamic type. Definition/allocation/inquiry premises remain necessary for any later finite observation.
External type-parameter changes are not an independent data representation, KIND-number or C descriptor contract.
External bounds changes do not define the bounds of an unallocated object or create a Fortran allocation operation in this source packet.
This excludes the INTENT(IN) dummy entity, including a pointer dummy; the separate ability to modify a live target through an IN pointer does not exempt that dummy.
The restriction is on specifying the attribute in the accessing context, not a blanket ban on using an already-volatile coarray supplied by its defining scope.

7.5.1p5/3.30.3 follow nonpointer component paths, including allocatable paths. A pointer-only route to a target with a coarray is not automatically this entity's coarray potential subobject component.
Coarray/coarray-potential-subobject status and USE/HOST access qualify the specification restriction. Different associated objects and local shadow declarations must not be conflated.
Use the actual19.4p3 construct-entity definition. A BLOCK USE statement creates construct entities, but its coarray access still has C871's separate specification restriction.
Original PDF134 combines a noncoarray association permission, the scoped BLOCK attribute effect and two canonical coarray-association cross-references.

Noncoarray objects can be associated across different VOLATILE attributes, subject to the actual route's constraints. In particular, a noncoarray with a coarray potential subobject is still subject to15.5.2.5p22's VOLATILE equivalence for dummy association.
This does not waive the actual/dummy, coindexed, contiguity, VALUE, definition, aliasing or other attribute restrictions, and supplies no blanket copy-in/copy-out or hardware-ordering promise.

14.2.2p2/p9/p10 govern local specification and multiple paths; C871 still forbids the qualified coarray/coarray-potential-subobject specification. Use-associated objects are already declared, not redeclared locally as fresh variables.
19.5.1.4 and8.8 govern host access and shadowing. A separate VOLATILE statement can qualify the host object locally; a new type declaration can instead introduce another object.
The outside object need not have the attribute. This local effect neither globally redeclares it nor says an existing outside attribute disappears.

15.5.2.9p1 requires corresponding coarray actual/dummy VOLATILE equivalence.15.5.2.5p22 additionally handles a dummy with a coarray potential subobject. These owners and their finite association mechanisms remain pending, not duplicated as local S executions.

10.2.2.3p7 requires pointer/target VOLATILE equivalence when the target is a coarray. This mandatory canonical condition is stronger than p3's general recommendation and does not require an external event.
Original PDF134 contains two should recommendations around one conditional shall. Their modalities and antecedents remain separate.
Giving a pointer VOLATILE when its target has VOLATILE is recommended, not by itself a universal local shall. Actual coarray targets retain the independent10.2.2.3p7 requirement.
The explicit target-attribute premise belongs to the first recommendation. It is not substituted for the following sentence's actual external-reference/definition/undefinition premise.
The mandatory branch is about an actual external target event. Neither a VOLATILE spelling, an ordinary Fortran assignment nor an unexecuted C-looking stub independently proves that event.
The all-members EQUIVALENCE guidance is a should, not mandatory attribute propagation to every storage-associated object and not the p4 subobject rule.
The recommendation is conditional on a member's VOLATILE attribute. Actual EQUIVALENCE/storage-association validity and definedness retain their canonical sources.

Apply3.138 and9.4.2p5: a rightmost sole pointer component is a subobject only in association-status contexts. Dereferenced targets and paths through an earlier pointer are not subobjects of that base object.

Original PDF134 recommends current-value use and prompt availability to non-Fortran parts. Both clauses use should, not shall. These are neither mandatory performance/visibility thresholds nor informative NOTE text.
Using the most recent definition is recommended. No mandatory processor pass/fail requirement is generated from this advisory wording.
The recommendation applies each time the object's value is required; no particular compiler optimization, memory barrier or read-count oracle is specified.
The second recommendation concerns a definition performed by Fortran and availability to the non-Fortran parts, not a portable C ABI, descriptor or atomicity contract.
As soon as possible supplies no numeric latency limit, synchronization event, compulsory operating-system interface or permission to turn sleep-based observations into conformance failures.

requirements.title: VOLATILE applies to a variable other than an INTENT(IN) dummy
requirements.definition: The VOLATILE entity is a variable and is not an INTENT(IN) dummy argument. The exclusion applies to a pointer dummy as well as a nonpointer dummy; target operations permitted through an IN pointer do not remove the dummy-attribute restriction.

pending.ordinary-variable-admission: PENDING complete ordinary INTEGER scalar/array/data-pointer/allocatable declarations, without INTENT(IN), invalid coarray association or unsupported component-attribute spelling. Compile admissions establish neither external changes nor runtime visibility.
pending.intent-in-data-exclusion: PENDING a complete ordinary INTEGER INTENT(IN),VOLATILE dummy declaration, repaired only by removing VOLATILE. No dummy definition or unavailable actual data is needed to violate the attribute constraint.
pending.intent-in-pointer-exclusion: PENDING the analogous data-pointer dummy declaration and one-attribute repair, with no target access or actual/dummy mismatch. Do not waive C870 because IN restricts pointer association rather than every target operation.
pending.nonvariable-role-source-boundary: PENDING named-constant/procedure/data-object classification and exact competing grammar/attribute constraints. Do not claim a uniquely isolated C870 report from an arbitrary PARAMETER or PROCEDURE rejection without independent cause/owner adjudication.

requirements.oracle: Complete variable declarations and minimally repaired INTENT(IN) conflicts, with independent subject-role and source-origin review. All new plans are pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting is not forced rejection, exact English or printed-code policy. Do not require a runtime trap, inspect an undefined pointer or credit generic unsupported-variable/attribute diagnostics.

requirements.title: USE or HOST access restricts new VOLATILE specification for coarray-bearing objects
requirements.definition: VOLATILE is not specified locally for a use- or host-associated coarray, or a variable with a coarray potential subobject component. Inherited attributes are distinct from the prohibited local specification. Potential-subobject membership follows the actual nonpointer component paths.

pending.use-associated-coarray-exclusion: PENDING a complete module and accessing procedure containing a separate VOLATILE statement for the use-associated coarray, repaired only by removing that statement. Preserve legitimate coarray storage/role and actual compiler/coarray support; a missing module or unsupported coarray is not the cause.
pending.host-associated-coarray-exclusion: PENDING a complete host/internal-procedure counterpart with the same coarray identity and a local VOLATILE statement. Do not introduce a local type declaration that shadows the host entity.
pending.use-associated-component-exclusion: PENDING a use-associated noncoarray variable of a valid type with an allocatable coarray potential subobject, including a source-reviewed nested nonpointer path. Keep component/coarray declaration restrictions valid and repair only the prohibited specification.
pending.host-associated-component-exclusion: PENDING the corresponding actual host-associated object and minimal local-specification repair. A pointer-only path to another object's coarray must not substitute for the required potential subobject.
pending.inherited-attribute-boundary: PENDING admission/source relations for a legitimately VOLATILE coarray declared in its defining scope and accessed without an added VOLATILE statement. C871 is not a blanket ban on accessing that entity; preserve14.2.2's multiple-path qualifications.
pending.pointer-path-source-boundary: PENDING exact3.30.3/7.5.1p5 nonpointer-path classification and finite qualified controls. Do not treat a target behind a pointer component as a coarray potential subobject of the parent or use an unassociated pointer dereference as evidence.

requirements.oracle: Distinct USE and HOST specification contrasts on real coarray/coarray-potential-subobject subjects, with valid minimal controls and explicit source relationships.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compiler run or capability profile is supplied here. Canonical module, host, coarray component, attribute and association conditions retain their owners. Silent acceptance or unrelated support/link failures are not successful reports.

requirements.title: BLOCK VOLATILE specification distinguishes construct entities from enclosing coarray-bearing objects
requirements.definition: Inside BLOCK, VOLATILE is not specified for a coarray or a variable with a coarray potential subobject component unless that entity is a construct entity of the BLOCK. This condition does not override C871 or other declaration restrictions.

pending.enclosing-coarray-exclusion: PENDING an enclosing legitimate coarray and a BLOCK VOLATILE statement that does not otherwise declare it. Repair only the statement. Apply the actual inclusive-scope/construct-entity rules, rather than treating BLOCK as an internal subprogram's host-association route.
pending.enclosing-component-exclusion: PENDING the corresponding enclosing noncoarray object with a coarray potential subobject. Establish the nonpointer path and complete valid type before calibrating a report.
pending.declared-coarray-construct-control: PENDING a coarray genuinely declared inside the BLOCK with a valid ALLOCATABLE or other legitimate storage/role route, and VOLATILE there. A bare VOLATILE statement by itself does not introduce a construct entity.
pending.declared-component-construct-control: PENDING a properly declared BLOCK object with a valid coarray potential subobject type. Keep allocation/state/component conditions and C1107-C1110 valid; do not infer execution or remote-image behavior from compilation.
pending.use-created-construct-boundary: PENDING19.4p3's explicit USE-in-BLOCK construct-entity relation and C871's remaining prohibition. Being a construct entity satisfies only this part of C872 and does not make a use-associated coarray's VOLATILE respecification conforming.

requirements.oracle: Complete BLOCK/enclosing identity contrasts and legitimate construct declarations, with actual object ownership and narrowly located causes.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not force hidden host association, redeclare a shadow object as a repair, waive C871, or manufacture a coarray runtime/visibility observer. All facets remain pending.

requirements.title: A BLOCK specification gives a nonlocal object VOLATILE within that construct
requirements.definition: A VOLATILE specification in BLOCK applies within the construct to an object that is not a local variable of that BLOCK, including when the object lacks the attribute outside. It does not create a new object, propagate the specification globally, or remove an existing outside attribute. The qualified coarray exclusions still apply.

pending.enclosing-object-scoped-attribute: PENDING a finite source/attribute-use relation for an ordinary noncoarray enclosing object named in a BLOCK VOLATILE statement. There is no portable IS_VOLATILE inquiry; an I/O-free declaration or unchanged printed value is not an independent runtime-effect test.
pending.associated-object-scoped-attribute: PENDING actual USE/HOST/inclusive-scope identity relations under14.2.2/19.5.1.4/19.4 and the coarray-potential-subobject exclusions. Use a separate attribute statement, not a type redeclaration creating a shadow object.
pending.outside-scope-nonpropagation: PENDING source/interface evidence distinguishing the inside specification from the unchanged outside context, including an already-volatile outside object. Do not infer attribute removal or a mandatory optimization change on leaving BLOCK.
pending.declaration-and-import-boundaries: PENDING11.1.4p2/19.4p3/8.8 relations for construct declarations, USE-created entities and IMPORT visibility. Real finite meta-evidence support is required before these source plans earn coverage.

requirements.oracle: A source/interface/attribute mechanism with a declared finite denominator and independently established identity; no no-op or generic timing loop substitutes for that mechanism.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No implementation is supplied. Recommendations about recent values or prompt external availability do not make a mandatory visibility/performance oracle for this scoped-attribute effect.

requirements.title: Actual external target events require the pointer to be VOLATILE
requirements.source: 8.5.20 p3 conditional shall sentence, physical PDF134
requirements.definition: If the pointer's target is referenced, defined or made undefined by means not specified by the program, the pointer has VOLATILE. These actual events, not merely a target attribute spelling, are the conditional premise. The adjacent general pointer and EQUIVALENCE advice remains recommendations.

pending.external-reference-premise: PENDING independently justified processor/environment evidence for an actual target reference by external means and the matching pointer attribute/source relationship. An ordinary call name, an unexecuted stub or a target's VOLATILE declaration does not establish the event.
pending.external-definition-premise: PENDING a bounded externally defined live target protocol with explicit data/association/lifetime premises and finite source/processor evidence. Do not substitute an ordinary Fortran assignment, a remote-image definition or a successful compiler run as the external-means oracle.
pending.external-undefinition-premise: PENDING a source/context-only demonstration of the actual external event and required declaration. Never read the undefined target afterward or require a compiler/runtime trap for violating this nonnumbered conditional obligation.
pending.coarray-equivalence-source-boundary: PENDING the independently owned10.2.2.3p7 pointer/coarray-target VOLATILE equivalence, which holds regardless of the external-event premise. Do not convert p3's noncoarray recommendation into that stronger mandatory rule.

requirements.oracle: Content-bound external-premise and pointer-attribute evidence, with context-only handling of invalid/undefined states. No external protocol or executable fixture is approved by this source catalogue.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The source does not require compile-time detection of an arbitrary external event. It supplies no descriptor ABI, atomicity, synchronization, exact latency or safe undefined-value inquiry. The first sentence's target-VOLATILE recommendation is not merged with this separate shall.

requirements.title: VOLATILE propagates to the object's actual subobjects
requirements.definition: Every subobject of a VOLATILE object also has VOLATILE. Actual subobject status is context dependent for pointer components: a rightmost sole pointer is a subobject for association-status purposes, but its dereferenced target is not a subobject of that base. A path through an earlier pointer likewise does not supply propagation from the original base.

pending.array-subobjects: PENDING finite actual element/section source relationships and an independently justified attribute observer. Index validity, ordinary value definedness and zero-size boundaries remain explicit; merely printing an unchanged element supplies no VOLATILE-effect proof.
pending.character-substring: PENDING a valid substring relation, with exact parent/substring identity and a finite attribute mechanism. Zero length is always defined but does not by itself observe propagation or external visibility.
pending.nonpointer-component-path: PENDING direct and nested nonpointer component relations, including valid allocated component contexts. Preserve declaration/accessibility/allocation premises; the parent and its target behind a pointer are not interchangeable.
pending.pointer-association-context: PENDING9.4.2p5's rightmost-sole-pointer association-status context with a defined status and a content-bound attribute relation. Do not inspect an undefined association or turn an allocated target's value into an association-status oracle.
pending.pointer-dereference-boundary: PENDING exact source/control relationships for a dereferenced pointer target and an intervening pointer in a longer path. Neither is a subobject of the original base for this propagation rule; other VOLATILE recommendations or coarray obligations keep their own owners.

requirements.oracle: Finite, independently reviewed subobject and attribute-use evidence, with context and lifetime bound to the actual entities; no synthetic passing program or unqualified optimization experiment.
requirements.oracle_limitation: There is no implemented general attribute-use evidence mechanism for these facets. No new SourceUses inventory, case link, compiler observation or passing effect is claimed. The EQUIVALENCE recommendation and p5 processor advice are not mandatory subobject propagation.

External possibilities are not compulsory events or ABI/atomicity/latency promises. C870excludesINpointerdummies too;C871andC872retain actual USE/HOST/BLOCK construct identity and coarray-potential-subobject conditions. Noncoarray permission does not waive15.5.2.5p22orcoarray dummy/pointer equivalence. Rightmost sole pointer components are subobjects for association-status purposes, not dereferenced targets.
